Rashi on Shabbat 156b:10:1.hebrew: תרגמא זעירי - במסכת ביצה, בבהמת קדשים, דאסורה בהנאה ולא חזיא לכלבים. הא דחולין, שפיר דמי להאכילה לכלבים:
Rashi on Shabbat 156b:10:1.english: Ze'eiri explained it - In Tractate Beitzah, [as referring] to a consecrated animal, which is forbidden for benefit and is not fit for dogs. However, [in the case of] a non-sacred [animal], it is well [permitted] to feed it to dogs.

Rashi on Shabbat 156b:1:1.english: Because Jupiter is situated - which is your constellation.

Rashi on Shabbat 156b:1:2.hebrew: במערב - שהוא מקום מצונן, ואין ראוי להוליד. כך מצאתי בהש"ס רבינו הלוי:
Rashi on Shabbat 156b:1:2.english: In the west - For it is a cold place, and is not fit for begetting [children]. Thus I found in the Talmud of Rabbeinu HaLevi.

Rashi on Shabbat 156b:1:3.english: In its east - For it is a place of heat.

Rashi on Shabbat 156b:1:4.english: Tzedek [Jupiter] - The Holy One, blessed be He, called it to bring it to the east.

Rashi on Shabbat 156b:1:5.english: To his foot - For his sake.

Rashi on Shabbat 156b:2:1.english: Ablet - [This] was the name of a gentile sage, and [he was] an astrologer.

Rashi on Shabbat 156b:2:2.hebrew: אזיל ואתי - דאין מזל לישראל, ויועיל לו תפלה:
Rashi on Shabbat 156b:2:2.english: He will go and come back - For there is no constellation for Israel, and prayer will avail him.

Rashi on Shabbat 156b:3:1.english: In two pieces - In two pieces, for he cut it along with the reeds without knowing.

Rashi on Shabbat 156b:3:2.hebrew: מרמינן בהדדי - מטילין פת [לסל] לכל החבורה כאחד, ואוכלין יחד, והאחד גובה מכולן:
Rashi on Shabbat 156b:3:2.english: We cast together - [They] cast bread [into a basket] for the entire group as one, and eat together, and one [person] collects from all of them.

Rashi on Shabbat 156b:3:3.english: I will arise and collect - I will collect [the bread] and place [it] in the basket.

Rashi on Shabbat 156b:3:4.english: I rendered myself as one who was taking from him - I made myself as one collecting from him, and I gave his portion from my own.

Rashi on Shabbat 156b:3:5.hebrew: לא ממיתה משונה - ומיהו מיתה הגונה ימות, אלא ממיתה עצמה מצלת ונותנת חיים:
Rashi on Shabbat 156b:3:5.english: Not from an unusual death - [Meaning, not that it saves only from an unusual death] and nevertheless he will die a natural death; rather, it saves from death itself and grants life.

Rashi on Shabbat 156b:4:2.english: She stuck it - She thrust it.

Rashi on Shabbat 156b:4:3.hebrew: למכבנתא - [אישפינגלי"ז בלע"ז], נושקא של זהב שיש כמו טס בראשה:
Rashi on Shabbat 156b:4:3.english: The pin - [Espingles in Old French], a golden brooch [nosche] that has something like a thin plate at its head.

Rashi on Shabbat 156b:5:1.english: My portion - [In Old French:] amenestraison [a served portion].

Rashi on Shabbat 156b:6:1.english: And pray for mercy - Ask for mercy so that the evil inclination will not rule over you.

Rashi on Shabbat 156b:6:2.hebrew: קיבורא - אשכול תמרים, והדקל לא שלו היה:
Rashi on Shabbat 156b:6:2.english: Kibura - A cluster of dates, and the palm tree was not his.

Rashi on Shabbat 156b:7:1.hebrew: את הדלועין - התלושין, ומיהו סתמן לאו למאכל בהמה קיימי, אלא לאדם:
Rashi on Shabbat 156b:7:1.english: The pumpkins - [That are] detached [from the ground]; however, ordinarily they are not designated for animal food, rather for human [consumption].

Rashi on Shabbat 156b:7:2.hebrew: ואת הנבלה - שנתנבלה היום, ובין השמשות היתה עומדת לאדם, ואפ"ה מחתכין:
Rashi on Shabbat 156b:7:2.english: And the carcass - That became a carcass today [on Shabbat], and at twilight it was designated for human [consumption], and even so one may cut [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 156b:8:1.hebrew: כר"ש - דלית ליה מוקצה:
Rashi on Shabbat 156b:8:1.english: In accordance with Rabbi Shimon - Who does not hold [the prohibition of] muktzeh.

Rashi on Shabbat 156b:9:1.hebrew: מדכרכי דזוזי - מחצלות העשויות לספינות לכסות פרקמטיא שבתוכן. זוזי — ספינות בלשון ארמי, כך מצאתי בתשובת הגאונים:
Rashi on Shabbat 156b:9:1.english: From [the case of] the mats of ships - Mats made for ships to cover the merchandise within them. Zuzei [means] ships in the Aramaic language; thus I found in a responsum of the Geonim.

Rashi on Shabbat 156b:9:2.english: When they would bring a tereifa before him - [This refers to] an animal regarding which a question of tereifut arose, and which requires the ruling of a Sage.

Rashi on Shabbat 156b:9:3.hebrew: אקלקילתא - על האשפה, שאם יראנה טריפה, יניחה שם:
Rashi on Shabbat 156b:9:3.english: On a garbage heap - On the garbage heap, so that if he sees it [to be] a tereifa, he will leave it there.

Rashi on Shabbat 156b:9:4.english: And it is not suited even for dogs - Because it was slaughtered today and they will not be able to move [it], in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda.

Tosafot on Shabbat 156b:10:1.hebrew: תרגמא זעירי בבהמת קדשים - תימה לר"י: היכי מוכח מהכא דס"ל כר"ש? ע"כ איצטריך לאוקמה בבהמת קדשים, כדמוכח פרק אין צדין (ביצה דף כז:), משום דמתני' נמי דיקא, דקתני עלה: "ולא החלה שנטמאת" — מה חלה דקדשים, אף בהמה דקדשים! ומכח האי דיוקא פריך התם למר בר אמימר, דאמר: "מודה היה ר"ש בבעלי חיים שמתו שאסורין". ודחיק ר"י לתרץ: דהכי קים ליה להש"ס שלא פירש זעירי כן אלא משום דבעי לאוקמה כר"ש. מ"ר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 156b:10:1.english: Ze’eiri explained it [as referring] to a consecrated animal - This is puzzling to the Ri: how is it proven from here that [Ze’eiri] holds in accordance with Rabbi Shimon? Perforce, it was necessary to establish [the Mishnah] as referring to a consecrated animal, as is proven in the chapter Ein Tzadin (Beitzah 27b), because the Mishnah itself also implies [this], as it teaches in the same passage: "Nor the challah that became ritually impure" — just as challah is of consecrated items, so too the animal is of consecrated items! And by force of this inference, [the Gemara] raises an objection there against Mar bar Ameimar, who said: "Rabbi Shimon concedes regarding living creatures that died that they are forbidden." And the Ri answers with difficulty that the Gemara was certain that Ze’eiri only explained it thus because he wanted to establish it in accordance with Rabbi Shimon. [From] my teacher:

Tosafot on Shabbat 156b:10:2.hebrew: והא א"ר יוחנן הלכה כסתם משנה ותנן אין מבקעין כו' - תימה לר"י: היכי מוכח מהכא דלא ס"ל כר"ש, דההיא ודאי כרבי יהודה? דשמא אית ליה לרבי יוחנן "מיגו דאיתקצאי לבין השמשות איתקצאי לכולי יומא"; וקורה שנשברה אפילו לר"ש איתקצאי בין השמשות קודם שבירתה, דהואי מוקצה מחמת חסרון כיס, דמודה ביה ר"ש; אבל במתניתין לא איתקצאי בין השמשות, דלית ליה ההיא מוקצה מה שהיא עומדת לאדם. והיה רוצה רבי לתרץ, דאי אית ליה לר' יוחנן "מיגו דאיתקצאי", היה אוסר ודאי לטלטל בהמה שנתנבלה בשבת — שהרי נהי שהיתה ראויה לכלבים בלא שחיטה כדפירשית לעיל, מיהו לטלטל היתה אסורה, דכולי עלמא מודו דבעלי חיים הם מוקצים, הוה לן למימר "מיגו דאיתקצאי". ודנתי לפני רבי: כיון שהיא ראויה לכלבים, משום שהיא מוקצה לטלטל אין לנו לאוסרה לטלטל נבלה בשבת; מידי דהוה אפירות הנושרין, דתלינן טעמא בריש ביצה (דף ג.) שמא יעלה ויתלוש, ומשום מוקצה לא אסירי לטלטל כיון דחזו לעורבים בעודן מחוברין, אע"פ שבעת חבורן היו אסורין לטלטל. ותירץ רבי: דמסתמא מתניתין בכל ענין איירי, בין אותן שראויין לכלבים בעודן חיים בין שאינן ראויין לכלבים, דבכולהו שרי ר"ש, ואכולהו קאי רבי יוחנן דאמר "הלכה כרבי שמעון" דמתניתין, ולא למחצה — אלמא לית ליה "מיגו דאיתקצאי". מ"ר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 156b:10:2.english: "Didn't Rabbi Yoḥanan say: The halakha is in accordance with an unattributed mishna, and we learned: One may not chop [wood], etc." - This is astonishing to Rabbi Yitzḥak [the Ri]: How is it proven from here that he [Rabbi Yoḥanan] does not hold in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, [on the grounds] that that [mishna] is certainly in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda? For perhaps Rabbi Yoḥanan holds [the principle]: "Since it was set aside at twilight, it is set aside for the entire day"; and a beam that broke was set aside at twilight before it broke even according to Rabbi Shimon, because it was muktzeh due to [fear of] monetary loss, which Rabbi Shimon concedes; whereas in our mishna it was not set aside at twilight, because he does not hold of that [category of] muktzeh [for] that which stands for human [use]. And my master wanted to answer that if Rabbi Yoḥanan held "since it was set aside," he would certainly forbid moving an animal that became a carcass on Shabbat — for although it was fit for dogs without slaughter, as I explained above, nevertheless it was forbidden to be moved [while alive], for everyone agrees that living creatures are muktzeh; [thus] we would have to say "since it was set aside." And I argued before my master: Since it is fit for dogs, merely because it is muktzeh with respect to moving [while alive], we should not forbid moving the carcass on Shabbat; just like fallen fruit, where we attribute the reason at the beginning of Beitzah (3a) to [the concern] "lest he climb and pluck [it]," and they are not forbidden to be moved on account of muktzeh since they were fit for ravens while still attached, even though while attached they were forbidden to be moved. And my master answered: Presumably our mishna speaks of every case — both those [animals] that are fit for dogs while alive and those that are not fit for dogs — for in all of them Rabbi Shimon permits [moving the carcass], and Rabbi Yoḥanan, who said "the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Shimon" of our mishna, refers to all of them and not to half [of them]; thus [it is proven that] he does not hold "since it was set aside." [From my master.]

Tosafot on Shabbat 156b:10:3.hebrew: והא אמר רבי יוחנן הלכה כסתם משנה - בריש ביצה (דף ב.) אמרינן גבי שבת דסתם לן תנא כר"ש, משמע דחשיב לסתמא דמתני' סתמא. אמר רבי: לאו משום סתמא קאמר, דודאי לא חשיב כסתמא, כיון דבמתניתין נמי פליג רבי יהודה; וסתמא לאו דוקא, אלא חשיב כרבים. מ"ר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 156b:10:3.english: And didn't Rabbi Yochanan say: The halakha is in accordance with an unattributed Mishnah - At the beginning of [Tractate] Beitzah (2a), we say regarding Shabbat that the Tanna taught an unattributed [Mishnah] in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, implying that [the Gemara] considers the anonymous [ruling] of our Mishnah to be an unattributed [Mishnah]. Rabbi said: It does not mean [that it is followed] because of [its being] an unattributed [Mishnah], for it is certainly not considered an unattributed [Mishnah], since in the Mishnah Rabbi Yehudah also disagrees; and [calling it] an "unattributed [Mishnah]" is imprecise, rather it is considered like [the view of] the majority. [From my teacher.]

Tosafot on Shabbat 156b:4:1.hebrew: כלדאי - בכולה סוגיא משמע דהיינו חוזים בכוכבים, ולא כמו שפירש"י בערבי פסחים (דף קיג:): "מניין שאין שואלין בכלדאים, שנאמר 'תמים תהיה' וגו'", ופירש דהיינו אוב. ועוד קשה, דבהדיא כתיב: "אל תפנו וגו'". ובספרי דרש: "מנין שאין שואלין בגורלות, שנאמר 'תמים תהיה'", וגורל וחוזה בכוכבים חדא מילתא היא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 156b:4:1.english: Kalda'ei [Chaldean astrologers] - Throughout the entire sugya, it is implied that they are stargazers, and not as Rashi explained in [the chapter] Arvei Pesachim (113b) [on the passage]: "From where [do we derive] that one may not consult Chaldeans? As it is stated: 'You shall be wholehearted [with the Lord your God]' etc." [Deuteronomy 18:13], where he explained that this refers to a necromancer (ov). Furthermore, [Rashi's explanation] is difficult, for it is explicitly written: "Do not turn [to the ovot] etc." [Leviticus 19:31]. And in the Sifrei it expounds: "From where [do we derive] that one may not consult lots? As it is stated: 'You shall be wholehearted'" — and [consulting] lots and stargazing are one and the same matter.

Tosafot on Shabbat 156b:7:1.hebrew: רבי יהודה אומר אם לא היתה נבלה מע"ש כו' - תימה: היכי מוכח בפסחים פרק מקום שנהגו בסופו (דף נו: ושם) ובפ"ק דביצה (דף ו: ושם) מהך מתניתין דמוכן לאדם לא הוי מוכן לכלבים? לעולם מוכן לאדם הוי מוכן לכלבים, והכא היינו טעמא דאסירא לכלבים — משום דהואי מוקצה מחמת איסור, שלא היתה ראויה חיה (לא) לאדם (ולא לכלבים)! ותירץ ר"י, דיש דברים ראויים ליתן לפני הכלבים חיים, כגון עופות וכיוצא בהן; הלכך אי לאו דמוכן לאדם לא הוי מוכן לכלבים, הוה שריא ליתן לכלבים. וה"ר יצחק בן הר"ר מאיר גריס במתני': "אם לא היתה נבלה מעיו"ט אסורה". השתא אתי שפיר בפשיטות, דמוכן שפיר לאדם ואינו מוקצה מחמת איסור. ולא נהירא לי, דבריש ביצה (דף ב.) דייק מינה דגבי שבת סתם לה תנא כר"ש; אלמא גבי שבת מיתניא. וה"ר פורת מפרש דממשנה יתירה דייק, דה"ל למתני "אם לא היתה נבלה מע"ש אסורה" ותו לא, דמאי צ"ל "לפי שאינה מן המוכן"? אלא להכי תני לה, דאפילו הוי מוכן לאדם לגמרי שלא היה מוקצה מחמת איסור — לא הוי מוכן לכלבים. מ"ר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 156b:7:1.english: Rabbi Yehudah says: If it was not a carcass from the eve of Shabbat, etc. - It is puzzling: how is it proven in Pesachim, [in] the chapter Makom SheNahagu, at its end (56b, and there [in the parallel]), and in the first chapter of Beitzah (6b, and there), from this Mishnah that what is prepared for a human is not [considered] prepared for dogs? [Perhaps] in general, what is prepared for a human is [also] prepared for dogs, and here this is the reason it is prohibited for dogs: because it was muktzeh on account of a prohibition, since while alive it was (not) fit for a human (and not for dogs)! And R"I answered that there are things fit to be placed before dogs while alive, such as birds and the like; therefore, were it not that what is prepared for a human is not [considered] prepared for dogs, it would be permitted to place [it] before dogs. And R. Yitzchak ben R. Meir reads in the Mishnah: "If it was not a carcass from the eve of Yom Tov, it is prohibited." Now it works out well simply, for it is properly prepared for a human [on Yom Tov] and is not muktzeh on account of a prohibition. But this does not appear [correct] to me, for at the beginning of Beitzah (2a) [the Gemara] infers from it that with respect to Shabbat the Tanna taught anonymously in accordance with Rabbi Shimon; thus, it was taught with respect to Shabbat. And R. Porat explains that [the Gemara] infers [it] from the superfluous [wording in the] Mishnah: for it should have taught "If it was not a carcass from the eve of Shabbat, it is prohibited," and nothing more — for why did it need to say "because it is not of that which is prepared"? Rather, it taught this to [indicate] that even if it were completely prepared for a human, such that it was not muktzeh on account of a prohibition, it is [still] not [considered] prepared for dogs. [From my teacher]:

Tosafot on Shabbat 156b:8:1.hebrew: ושמואל אמר הלכה כר"ש - תימה לר"י: תרתי דשמואל למה לי? דתיפוק ליה מההיא דכרכי דזוזי, ועז לחלבה, ורחל לגיזתה, דשילהי פ"ק (דף יט: ושם). ותירץ ר"י דמוקצה דהתם קיל ממוקצה דהכא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 156b:8:1.english: And Shmuel said: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Shimon - It is puzzling to R. Yitzchak: Why do I need two [statements] of Shmuel? Let him derive it from that [teaching] regarding bundles of zuzim [coins], a goat for its milk, and a ewe for its shearing, at the end of the first chapter (19b, and there). And R. Yitzchak answered that the muktzeh there is more lenient than the muktzeh here.
